_setup: Static-token Atlassian MCP for HEADLESS / scheduled routines (Path A of loop-engineering).
The claude.ai OAuth connector does NOT survive a scheduled run (token is in-memory per
session; a fresh scheduled connection is unauthenticated). This registers Atlassian's
official Rovo MCP server in API-token mode, which authenticates from a static header and
1. Generate an Atlassian Cloud API token at https://id.atlassian.com/manage-profile/security/api-tokens
2. An org admin must enable token auth: Atlassian Administration -> Rovo -> Rovo MCP server
-> Authentication -> allow API token. (Without this, only OAuth works.)
3. Build the Basic credential WITHOUT committing the token:
Put that export in the routine's env (or your shell profile for interactive use).
4. Copy the mcpServers block below into your HOST project's .mcp.json (NOT the plugin repo).
5. The token is NOT bound to a cloudId — atlassian-expert resolves it via
getAccessibleAtlassianResources on first use and threads it through calls.
6. Delete this _setup key from the real .mcp.json (it is ignored, but keep the file clean).
This server registers under the key 'atlassian' -> tools are mcp__atlassian__<tool>, the
SAME base names as the OAuth connector. atlassian-expert is dual-bound to both prefixes.
